Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a road traffic accident, filed application under Sec.166 of I.M.V.Act, claiming compensation worth Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA-1141, alleging that on 16.09.2021 at about 7 p.m., when driving Maruthi Omni car bearing No.KA-04-MF-6438 from Kabbalu towards Bengaluru, on Sathanur-Kanakapura NH-209, near petrol bunk, Shivanahalli village, Kanakapura Taluk, rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-08-EA-1141 rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the car, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Regarding the accident, Kanakapura Traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.29/2021 against the rider of the motorcycle.
Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Kanakapura and Nano Hospital, Bengaluru, by spending Rs.2 Lakhs.
As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 19 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/- p.m., by working as a driver.

3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2/insurance company appeared through his advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
4. The respondent No.2 denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground that as on the date of accident, the person who rode the motorcycle had no licence to ride the same.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 25.10.2022 this Authority has framed the following issues:-
1)Whether the petitioner proves that on 16.09.2021 at about 7.00 pm near petrol bunk , Shivanahalli village on NH-209 road (Sathanoor - Kanakapura road) in Kanakapura of Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, he being the driver of the Maruthi Omni bearing reg.No.KA-04-MF-6438 had met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-08-EA-1141 by its rider and he sustained injuries in the accident as averred ?
2) Whether respondent No.2 proves that this petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties ?
3)Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation ?
If so, what amount and from whom ?
4 ) What order ?
7. On 20.01.2023, 09.02.2023, 22.03.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 14 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.14.
On 21.06.2023 and 26.07.2023 petitioner produced evidence of Dr. Girish.G. as PW.2 and get produced 2 documents at Exs.P.15 & P.16.

REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence, petitioner stated that on on 16.09.2021 at about 7 p.m., when driving Maruthi Omni car bearing No.KA-04-MF-6438 from Kabbalu towards Bengaluru, on Sathanur-Kanakapura NH-209, near petrol bunk, Shivanahalli village, Kanakapura Taluk, rider of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-08-EA-1141 rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the car,
thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11.
In the written statement the respondent No.2/insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated that Kanakapura-Sathanoor main road is a heavy traffic area and he was driving the car from his house towards Kabbalamma temple.
Petitioner admitted that in the accident, front part of the Omni car has been damaged.
Petitioner stated that his elder brother Nithin has filed the complaint.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that he drove the car in high speed, met with self-accident and as the car had no RC and policy, implicated motorcycle by colluding with the police.
13.
In the evidence PW.2 Dr. Girish stated nothing regarding the reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Cr.No.29/2021 pertaining to Kanakapura Traffic Police station, registered against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA-1141 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC, on the basis of the complaint presented by Nithin S/o Lakshman - one of the inmates of the car.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar dated 17.09.2021.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the vehicle seizure mahazar dated 17.09.2021.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident report dated 18.09.2021 in which damage noticed by the Motor Vehicle Inspector in motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA-1141 and car bearing No.KA-04-MF-6438 are mentioned.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the wound certificate.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Kanakapura Traffic police in Cr.No.29/2021 against Jashwath Gowda @ Shashank s/o Siddaraju - Suresh Murugan Alias Suresh.M vs Suman.N on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190907866/

sentences.text: In the Discharge Summary, history of illness is noted as 'road traffic accident between two wheeler and four wheeler'.
In the file there are no evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 16.09.2021 at 7 p.m., when petitioner was driving the car bearing No.KA-04-MF-6438 from Kanakapura towards Bengaluru on Sathanoor- Kanakapura NH-209 near petrol bunk, Shivanahalli village, Kanakapura taluk, Jashwath Gowda s/o Siddaraju negligently rode the motorcycle bearing No. KA-08-EA-1141,
dashed the same to the car, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

15. Issue No.2 : In the written statement respondent No.2/insurance company asserted that the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties, thereby indirectly asserted that presence of the owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-04-MF-6438 are necessary to decide the case.

16. According to law for the time being in force, the respondent No.2 is having right and liberty and also having responsibility to take suitable steps to implead the person whose presence is necessary to decide the dispute.
In this case the respondent No.2 has not taken steps to implead any person to the case.

According to law for the time being in force, i.e., provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act, the presence of owner and insurer of the vehicle which according to the petitioner caused accident, are only necessary to decide the case.
Hence, I have inferred that the present petition is not bad for non-joinder of any other parties.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in the Negative.
17. Issue Nos.3 & 4:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident, he has suffered injury to occipital bone, multiple laceration over face and scalp and soft tissue injury in frontal region, took first aid at Government Hospital, Kanakapura and then took treatment at Nano Hospital,
Bengaluru, by spending Rs.2 Lakhs and require to take further treatment at the cost of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident, used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month by working as a driver.
18. In the written statement, respondent No.2/insurance company denied the allegation regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
19. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion about creation of the medical bills marked at Ex.P.11 for the purpose of this case.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that entire medical expenses are reimbursed from the medical insurance claim company.

Petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.2 Lakhs for treatment and non-requirement to take further treatment at the cost of Rs.One lakh.
20.
In the evidence, PW.2 Dr.Girish stated that on 26.05.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 8% to the whole body.

In the cross-examination PW.2 stated that he never treated the petitioner, however verified wound certificate, discharge summary, follow-up records during assessment of the quantum of Suresh Murugan Alias Suresh.M vs Suman.N on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190907866/

sentences.text: permanent physical disability of the petitioner.
PW.2 stated non-verification of the case sheet and old x-ray.
PW.2 submitted that the petitioner has suffered facial injuries and there is improvement in the health condition of the petitioner after discharge till recent examination.

21. Wound certificate, discharge summary, OPD records, medical bills, case sheet and other medical records shows that in the accident, petitioner suffered occipital bone fracture, multiple lacerations over face and scalp, took first aid at Government Hospital, Kanakapura, then took treatment at Nano Hospital, Bengaluru, as an inpatient from 16.09.2021 to 18.09.2021 by spending approximately Rs.49,900/-.
In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.

As the petitioner has suffered injuries to the face/occipital region, in the evidence PW.2 Dr. Girish submitted tat subsequent to discharge from the hospital till the date of examination, there is improvement in the health condition of the petitioner, I have inferred that the evidence placed by PW.2 are insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

Hence, I award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering,Rs.49,900/-
towards treatment charges, Rs.3,000/- towards attendant and conveyance charges, Rs.60,000/-
(15000 x 4months) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities and unhappiness.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle to receive a sum of Rs.1,97,900/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.

22. In the lengthy argument, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner by analysing the evidence available in the file, requested to pass order directing the respondent No.2/insurance company to deposit the compensation amount reserving liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA-1141 by relying on the Judgment dated17.05.2018 of the Apex Court reported in 2018 0 Supreme(SC) 490 (DB) (Amrit Paul Singh &
Anr. Vs. TATA AIG Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd.& Ors.)

As referred above, after investigation, police have filed the chargesheet alleging that Jashwath Gowda S/o Siddaraju-rider of the motorcycle and Suman S/o Nanjappa-owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA- 1141 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC Suresh Murugan Alias Suresh.M vs Suman.N on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190907866/

sentences.text: Hence, it is clear that as on the date of accident, Jashwath Gowda had no licence to ride motorcycle with gear and respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle has violated the terms of the policy.

As per the recent Judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka dated 14.12.2023 and 13.04.2023, the respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle who violated the terms of the driver clause of the policy, is not entitled to be indemnified by the respondent No.2/insurance company.
Hence, the respondent No.1 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of IMV Act, is partly allowed in the following terms:
The respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-08-EA-1141 shall pay Rs.1,97,900/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Seven Thousand Nine Hundred only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the petitioner towards compensation.
Respondents No.1 shall deposit compensation amount and interest within three months from today.
After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 8 th day of October, 2024.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.

Hence, I award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering,Rs.49,900/-
towards treatment charges, Rs.3,000/- towards attendant and conveyance charges, Rs.60,000/-
(15000 x 4months) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.35,000/- towards loss of amenities and unhappiness.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle to receive a sum of Rs.1,97,900/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.

As per the recent Judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka dated 14.12.2023 and 13.04.2023, the respondent No.1/owner of the motorcycle who violated the terms of the driver clause of the policy, is not entitled to be indemnified by the respondent No.2/insurance company.
Hence, the respondent No.1 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following:

After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
